title: Fixed variables survive the literal fold
statement: Let $\rho : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Option}\,\mathrm{Bool}$ be a restriction on $n$ variables, let $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be a Boolean assignment, and let $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_m$ be literals on these variables. Process the literals from left to right, starting from $\rho$: at each literal, if its variable is still free in the restriction accumulated so far, fix that variable to the value $x$ assigns it, and otherwise change nothing. Then any variable $v$ that already carries a fixed value under $\rho$ (that is, $\rho(v)$ leaves $v$ set rather than free) still carries a fixed value in the final restriction; the fold never frees an already-fixed variable.
hypotheses_covered: a list of literals on n variables
a restriction ρ on n variables
a Boolean assignment x : Fin n → Bool
a variable v that is fixed in ρ (ρ(v) ≠ none)
replaced:
If $\rho(v) \neq \mathrm{none}$, then after the $\mathrm{termSubTree}$ fold over $\mathit{lits}$ the
entry at $v$ remains non-\texttt{none}; that is, the fold never unsets an already-fixed variable.
